 Phoenix Suns 101 – 96 Charlotte Hornets Live Updated 3 minutes ago Suns vs Hornets LIVE, Score Updates and Play-by-Play in NBA (101-96)
 Follow Phoenix Suns vs Charlotte Hornets live from Mortgage Matchup Center: 2026-27 NBA score updates, Devin Booker box score stats and play-by-play.
 Coverage by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta Updated November 12, 2026, 11:31 pm ET ADVERTISEMENT
 FINAL Last update 11:31 PM ET 11:31 PM ET 3 minutes ago End of the game: Phoenix Suns defeats Charlotte Hornets 101-96
 The final buzzer sounds at Mortgage Matchup Center as Phoenix Suns closes out a 101-96 victory over Charlotte Hornets . Devin Booker (with 30 points and 7 assists) and Dillon Brooks (with 15 points) led the way for Phoenix Suns, while Coby White (with 21 points) and Naz Reid (with 16 points and 8 rebounds) paced Charlotte Hornets.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 Key moments
 11:31 PM ET End of the game: Phoenix Suns defeats… 
 10:52 PM ET End of the third quarter 
 10:16 PM ET Scoring leaders heading into the second half 
 10:08 PM ET Halftime at Mortgage Matchup Center 
 9:37 PM ET End of the first quarter at Mortgage Matchup… 
 8:28 PM ET Suns and Hornets 30 minutes from tip-off 
 Follow VAVEL on Google 11:30 PM ET 4 minutes ago Phoenix Suns hold the lead in the 4th quarter
 Miles Bridges cashes in 1 of 2 from the foul line. Devin Booker steps to the stripe and hits 2 of 2 from the foul line. That bucket pushes Devin Booker to 30 points on the night for Phoenix Suns .
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 11:26 PM ET 8 minutes ago O'Neale and Bridges add late free throws
 Royce O'Neale stepped to the line for a single free throw and buried it, giving the Phoenix Suns one more point in the closing seconds of the fourth quarter. Grayson Allen was then whistled for a foul, and Miles Bridges split his two attempts from the stripe. Play was also halted for a timeout at Mortgage Matchup Center during this sequence.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 11:22 PM ET 12 minutes ago Perimeter spacing opens the floor for Phoenix Suns
 Devin Booker knocks down a floater on the pass from Oso Ighodaro. Moussa Diabate connects on a layup off an assist from Grayson Allen. Devin Booker finishes with a three-pointer. Royce O'Neale scores on a three-pointer on the pass from Sion James. That bucket pushes Devin Booker to 28 points on the night for Phoenix Suns .
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 11:17 PM ET 17 minutes ago Dillon Brooks drills a big three for Phoenix
 Play is halted for a timeout at 2:01 of the fourth quarter after Dillon Brooks buried a three from the perimeter off an Oso Ighodaro feed, the only points the Phoenix Suns put up in this stretch. Royce O'Neale and Grayson Allen each gave the ball away for the Suns, while Moussa Diabate kept Charlotte alive with two offensive boards and a rejection of Ighodaro at the rim.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 11:12 PM ET 22 minutes ago Booker answers from mid-range
 Ryan Kalkbrenner found Grant Williams at the rim for an easy layup, but Grayson Allen replied for Phoenix with a pull-up two after Royce O'Neale cleared the defensive glass. Kalkbrenner and Khaman Maluach each pulled down a defensive board on the next trips, and once O'Neale was whistled for a foul, Devin Booker drilled a jumper from mid-range.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 11:07 PM ET 26 minutes ago Kennard answers every Charlotte push
 Luke Kennard scored twice for Phoenix in this stretch, first finishing a feed from Miles Bridges after Bridges cleaned up the defensive glass. Grayson Allen stripped Khaman Maluach and Royce O'Neale made Phoenix pay with a three off a Christian Anderson feed, but Kennard replied with a pull-up off a Maluach dish before Anderson coughed the ball up at the other end.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 11:04 PM ET 30 minutes ago Ighodaro throws it down as Phoenix punishes Reid
 Naz Reid coughed it up twice for Charlotte, traveling right after securing a defensive board and later losing the ball to a Miles Bridges strip. Phoenix cashed in both times, first with a Collin Gillespie mid-range jumper set up by Oso Ighodaro. Jordan Goodwin then kept the next possession alive on the offensive glass and lobbed one up for an Ighodaro alley-oop slam.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 11:00 PM ET 34 minutes ago Defensive stops at both ends at Mortgage Matchup Center
 Luke Kennard scores on a jumper off an assist from Oso Ighodaro. Coby White steps to the stripe and hits 2 of 2 from the foul line.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 10:56 PM ET 38 minutes ago Bridges and Gillespie pull Phoenix level
 Collin Gillespie grabbed the defensive board and found Miles Bridges cutting to the rim, and Bridges finished the layup through a Sion James foul before adding the free throw. James then gave the ball away on a traveling call, and Gillespie made Charlotte pay with a pull-up jumper. Naz Reid answered at the line, splitting a pair after Jordan Goodwin's foul.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 10:52 PM ET 42 minutes ago End of the third quarter
 The horn sounds on the third quarter at Mortgage Matchup Center, and the Charlotte Hornets carry a four-point edge over the Phoenix Suns into the fourth. Jordan Goodwin crashed the offensive glass in the closing stretch of the period to earn a second-chance possession.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 10:50 PM ET 44 minutes ago Half-court possessions between Suns and Hornets
 Christian Anderson connects on a three-pointer, set up by Grant Williams. Naz Reid converts 1 of 2 from the foul line after drawing the foul.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 10:45 PM ET an hour ago Phoenix Suns keep the cushion against Charlotte Hornets
 Khaman Maluach connects on a two-point basket. Play pauses for a timeout with 2:28 showing in the 3rd quarter.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 10:41 PM ET an hour ago Booker's pull-up answers Anderson's triple
 Devin Booker hit a mid-range jumper and later pulled up for two more to reach 21 points on the night for Phoenix. In between, Christian Anderson buried a perimeter three off a Grayson Allen pass for Charlotte, while Allen also gave the ball away on a traveling call. Ryan Dunn added two defensive rebounds in the stretch.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 10:37 PM ET an hour ago Dillon Brooks gives Phoenix a lift in the third
 Jalen Green got Phoenix going at the line with two free throws, and Dillon Brooks followed with a layup off a Devin Booker feed and a three on Oso Ighodaro's pass. Coby White answered for Charlotte with a triple set up by Grayson Allen and later a layup at the rim, while a Booker turnover handed the Hornets another possession.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 10:33 PM ET an hour ago Timeout on the floor in the 3rd quarter
 Devin Booker knocks down a jumper. Grayson Allen connects on a three-pointer off an assist from Sion James. Coby White finishes with a layup.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 10:28 PM ET an hour ago Clean look drops for Coby White in the 3rd quarter
 Naz Reid knocks down a two-point basket on the pass from Grayson Allen. Moussa Diabate connects on a tip-in. Dillon Brooks finishes with a layup, set up by Devin Booker. 3 points in a row for Coby White: a layup and a free throw.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 10:24 PM ET an hour ago Suns set the pace against Hornets
 Play continues with 11:57 on the third-quarter clock inside Mortgage Matchup Center as Phoenix Suns and Charlotte Hornets contest every possession. Devin Booker (Phoenix Suns: 15) and Coby White (Charlotte Hornets: 9) lead the statistical categories so far.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 10:16 PM ET an hour ago Scoring leaders heading into the second half
 For Phoenix Suns , the first-half scoring comes from Devin Booker (with 15 points and 5 assists), Jalen Green (with 10 points) and Collin Gillespie (with 9 points), while Charlotte Hornets gets its production from Coby White (with 9 points), Naz Reid (with 9 points) and Grayson Allen (with 9 points).
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 10:13 PM ET an hour ago Charlotte owns the glass at the break
 Khaman Maluach also got a hand on Moussa Diabate's attempt late in the 2nd quarter, the second stop at the rim before halftime. Phoenix shot 20-48 from the field and 10-27 from deep in the half, while Charlotte matched that 42% clip at 18-43 and won the boards 28 to 15. The Suns edged the assist column, 12 to 11.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 10:08 PM ET an hour ago Halftime at Mortgage Matchup Center
 Devin Booker closes the first half by rejecting Sion James at the rim, and the buzzer sends the Phoenix Suns into the locker room up five on the Charlotte Hornets at Mortgage Matchup Center. Booker has carried Phoenix through two quarters with 15 points and 5 assists. On the Charlotte side, Coby White tops the scoring sheet with 9 points.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 10:06 PM ET an hour ago Jalen Green answers with a pull-up
 Royce O'Neale sinks both free throws, and a foul on Christian Anderson sends Jalen Green to the line, where he splits the pair. After a Naz Reid turnover out of bounds, Green answers with a pull-up jumper and Reid scores from the floor. Grayson Allen, Dillon Brooks and Moussa Diabate grab defensive boards before Anderson is whistled again.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 10:02 PM ET 2 hours ago Bench rotation minutes underway in the 2nd quarter
 Royce O'Neale cashes in 1 of 2 from the foul line. Play pauses for a timeout with 3:12 showing in the 2nd quarter.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 9:57 PM ET 2 hours ago Phoenix Suns keep the cushion against Charlotte Hornets
 4 points in a row for Grant Williams: a three-pointer and a free throw. Devin Booker converts a layup, set up by Dillon Brooks. Sion James knocks down a layup on the pass from Christian Anderson. Grant Williams connects on a three-pointer.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 9:54 PM ET 2 hours ago Bridges and Ighodaro connect at the rim
 Devin Booker gives the ball away out of bounds and Sion James cleans up a defensive board, but after a few empty trips Oso Ighodaro finds Miles Bridges at the rim for a Phoenix Suns layup. Following whistles on Dillon Brooks and Ighodaro, James heads to the line for Charlotte and splits the pair.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 9:49 PM ET 2 hours ago Jordan Goodwin connects from beyond the arc
 Jordan Goodwin connects on a three-pointer, set up by Miles Bridges. Naz Reid finishes with a jumper. Luke Kennard scores on a jumper.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 9:45 PM ET 2 hours ago Perimeter spacing opens the floor for Phoenix Suns
 Collin Gillespie connects on a three-pointer, set up by Miles Bridges. Miles Bridges steps to the stripe and hits 2 of 2 from the foul line. Naz Reid finishes with a two-point basket on the pass from Coby White. Collin Gillespie scores on a three-pointer off an assist from Miles Bridges.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 9:40 PM ET 2 hours ago Gillespie stretches the Suns lead from deep
 Collin Gillespie punishes the Charlotte Hornets from beyond the arc off a feed from Luke Kennard, moments after Tidjane Salaun was whistled for a foul. Coby White answers with a bucket from the floor, and Miles Bridges keeps a later Charlotte possession alive with two straight offensive boards. White then coughs it up, and the Phoenix Suns get the ball back.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 9:37 PM ET 2 hours ago End of the first quarter at Mortgage Matchup Center
 Tidjane Salaun gets the last word of the opening quarter for Charlotte, crashing the offensive glass after a miss and hammering home a dunk on the second chance. That put-back trims the Phoenix Suns' edge to six heading into the second quarter at Mortgage Matchup Center.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 9:36 PM ET 2 hours ago Defensive stops at both ends at Mortgage Matchup Center
 Ryan Kalkbrenner steps to the stripe and hits 2 of 2 from the foul line. Devin Booker scores on a three-pointer.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 9:31 PM ET 2 hours ago Booker scores five straight and sets up Goodwin
 Christian Anderson buries a triple for Charlotte off a feed from Sion James, but Devin Booker answers right away from beyond the arc and follows it with a bucket from the floor. Booker then finds Jordan Goodwin for another three, and Phoenix takes this stretch 8-3 with Ryan Dunn adding a steal on Naz Reid along the way.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 9:27 PM ET 2 hours ago Jalen Green caps a 7-0 Suns burst
 Devin Booker gets Phoenix going with a midrange jumper, then cleans up the defensive glass at the other end. Jalen Green follows by sinking both free throws after a whistle on Royce O'Neale, and once Oso Ighodaro secures another stop, Booker kicks it to Green for a three that caps a 7-0 Suns stretch before a timeout.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 9:22 PM ET 2 hours ago Coby White converts on the offensive glass and midrange
 Coby White converts a three-pointer, set up by Naz Reid. Play pauses for a timeout with 6:20 showing in the 1st quarter.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 9:18 PM ET 2 hours ago Booker sets the table for Dillon Brooks
 Coby White and Moussa Diabate are finding each other for Charlotte, with White lobbing an alley-oop for a Diabate dunk and Diabate returning the favor on a White layup at the rim. Devin Booker answers with a triple and twice feeds Dillon Brooks, first for a layup and then for a three. Grayson Allen buries two shots from deep, one of them set up by Sion James.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 9:13 PM ET 2 hours ago Jalen Green cashes in on a Hornets turnover
 Moussa Diabate gives the ball away for Charlotte, and although Sion James cleans up the defensive glass on the next Phoenix trip, he loses the handle out of bounds moments later. Jalen Green punishes the second Hornets miscue, slicing to the rim and finishing a layup to get the Phoenix Suns on the board at Mortgage Matchup Center.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 9:12 PM ET 2 hours ago Even contest between Suns and Hornets
 Moussa Diabate pulls down the offensive rebound for a second-chance possession. Play continues with 11:27 on the first-quarter clock inside Mortgage Matchup Center as Phoenix Suns and Charlotte Hornets contest every possession. Sion James (Charlotte Hornets: 1) lead the statistical categories so far.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 9:01 PM ET 3 hours ago Latest injury report and availability update: Charlotte Hornets vs Phoenix Suns
 Here is the latest pregame availability and injury report ahead of Charlotte Hornets vs Phoenix Suns at Mortgage Matchup Center (Suns Live).
 Phoenix Suns injury report: Mark Williams (C) - Out.
 Charlotte Hornets injury report: Brandon Miller (F) - Out; Kon Knueppel (G) - Out; Dennis Schroder (G) - Out.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 8:52 PM ET 3 hours ago Teams back out at Mortgage Matchup Center ahead of tip-off
 Phoenix Suns and Charlotte Hornets take the court at Mortgage Matchup Center (Phoenix) (records: Phoenix Suns 4-6 , Charlotte Hornets 4-7 ) ahead of tip-off on Suns Live . Assigned officials: Scott Foster, Eric Dalen and Matt Myers .
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 8:44 PM ET 3 hours ago Suns and Hornets head back to the locker rooms
 With 15 minutes to go before tip-off, the Phoenix Suns and Charlotte Hornets have left the floor at the Mortgage Matchup Center and headed back to their locker rooms. Scott Foster, Eric Dalen and Matt Myers make up tonight's officiating crew, and the next stop for the Suns and Hornets are the arena walkout in Phoenix.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 8:36 PM ET 3 hours ago Suns and Hornets hit the floor in Phoenix
 The Phoenix Suns and Charlotte Hornets are out on the floor at the Mortgage Matchup Center, running through shooting and positional drills 20 minutes before tip-off. Brandon Miller carries the scoring load for a 4-7 Charlotte team at 20.6 points per game, while Devin Booker enters the night as the top scorer for the 4-6 Suns.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 8:28 PM ET 3 hours ago Suns and Hornets 30 minutes from tip-off
 We are 30 minutes away from tip-off at the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, where the Suns host the Charlotte Hornets with the broadcast on Suns Live . Phoenix walks onto its home floor with a 4-6 record, while Charlotte makes the trip carrying a 4-7 mark into tonight's meeting.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 8:25 PM ET 3 hours ago 35 minutes to tip-off in Phoenix
 The doors are open at the Mortgage Matchup Center and the Suns and Hornets are getting ready for a 9:00 p.m. ET tip-off.
 Starting lineups, the last injury confirmations and live scoring come next here on VAVEL.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 8:11 PM ET 3 hours ago Booker watch: 25.1 points and 4.8 assists per game
 Devin Booker is the best barometer of the game. When the Suns have scored 117 or more in this recent stretch (119, 117, 133), he has been central to the offense, and when they have dropped to 96 or 102, the creation load has been harder to carry.
 Expect the Hornets to send extra attention to him early.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 7:48 PM ET 4 hours ago Mark Williams is out for Phoenix
 Phoenix lists center Mark Williams as out with a shoulder injury. That puts more minutes on the remaining big men and on Miles Bridges, who leads the Suns with 7.4 rebounds per game.
 The Hornets have Moussa Diabate at 9.1 rebounds per game, the best rebounding average on either roster.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 7:29 PM ET 4 hours ago From 80 to 124: Charlotte's offensive swing in two games
 The Hornets scored 80 points against Boston and then 124 against Cleveland. That is a gap of 44 points between two games played only days apart.
 It is the best summary of how unpredictable this Charlotte offense has been, and tonight's depleted backcourt makes a repeat of the 124-point night harder to expect.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 7:07 PM ET 4 hours ago Phoenix is 4-3 at home and coming off a 23-point win
 The Suns have been better in front of their own fans, with a 4-3 home record and a 133-110 win over the Clippers in their latest game.
 That result came right after a 122-96 loss to San Antonio, so the team has shown it can bounce back quickly this month.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 7:06 PM ET 4 hours ago Hornets are 1-3 on the road this season
 Charlotte's away record is one of the clearest reasons Phoenix is favored. The Hornets have won only one of four road games, and the 114-104 loss at Brooklyn is the road game in their last five.
 Without Miller, Knueppel and Schroder, the road scoring problem is sharper tonight than it has been all season.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 6:00 PM ET 6 hours ago How to watch Hornets at Suns and tip-off time
 Tip-off at the Mortgage Matchup Center is scheduled for 9:00 p.m. ET, 8:00 p.m. CT, 7:00 p.m. in Phoenix and 02:00 GMT on Friday (03:00 in Madrid).
 Phoenix fans can watch locally on Arizona's Family 3TV or stream on Suns Live, and NBA League Pass carries the game for out-of-market viewers.
 Stay with VAVEL for confirmed starting lineups, live quarter-by-quarter scoring, Devin Booker's box score and the final injury updates on the Hornets' backcourt before the opening tip.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 6:00 PM ET 6 hours ago Phoenix, the Mortgage Matchup Center and season series
 The game is played at the Mortgage Matchup Center in downtown Phoenix, an arena also known in the local listing as Talking Stick Resort Arena. It is the Suns' home floor, where they are 4-3 this season.
 These two teams will meet twice in the regular season. Tonight is the first game of the series, and the rematch is set for March 13, 2027, in Charlotte at 6:00 p.m. ET, so tonight's result gives one side an early lead in the head-to-head. Both teams have won exactly four games so far, which makes the matchup a good measuring stick for where each one actually stands.
 Charlotte arrives on a 1-3 road record, so the Hornets still need to prove they can win consistently away from Charlotte.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 6:00 PM ET 6 hours ago The betting line: Phoenix by 6.5 with a total of 214.5
 The market sees this as a clear Phoenix edge. The Suns are listed as 6.5-point favorites, and the over/under sits at 214.5 points.
 The total is modest compared with the way the Suns scored in recent games (133 against the Clippers, 119 against Portland), but it also reflects the 96-point night against San Antonio and a Hornets offense that has been shorthanded. Charlotte also gave up 119 to Boston and 124 to Detroit in the past two weeks, so the defensive side of the total deserves attention too.
 The number to watch is the Charlotte shooting at the rim and from three: without Miller and Knueppel, their spacing is not what it was earlier in the season, and Phoenix can pack the paint more than usual.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 6:00 PM ET 6 hours ago Rebounding matchup: Bridges against Diabate
 One of the most interesting individual duels is on the boards. Miles Bridges averages 7.4 rebounds for Phoenix, while Moussa Diabate averages 9.1 for Charlotte, the highest team number on either roster.
 With Mark Williams sidelined for the Suns, Phoenix does not have its usual size on the interior, which puts a premium on defensive rebounding. For Charlotte, second-chance points are one of the few dependable sources of offense when Miller, Knueppel and Schroder are not available to create off the dribble.
 Keep an eye on offensive rebounds in the first quarter, because they usually tell us who has the edge inside.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 6:00 PM ET 6 hours ago Where both teams stand in the standings
 The table is tight at the bottom of two divisions. In the Pacific, the Los Angeles Lakers lead at 11-2, followed by Golden State at 8-4, Phoenix at 4-6, the Clippers at 2-8 and Sacramento at 1-10.
 In the Southeast, Atlanta tops the group at 7-5, Miami is 5-6, and Charlotte and Orlando are both 4-7, with Washington at 4-8.
 That means Phoenix sits third in its division, five and a half games behind the Lakers, while Charlotte is tied for third in the Southeast. A win in this one is worth more than a normal November game for two teams trying not to fall off the pace early.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 6:00 PM ET 6 hours ago Hornets last five: from an 80-point night to 124 against Cleveland
 Charlotte's recent run has been rough, yet it ended with a result worth noting. The Hornets lost 109-104 to Philadelphia, 124-91 to Detroit, 114-104 at Brooklyn and 119-80 to Boston.
 Then came a 124-112 win over Cleveland in their latest game, scoring 124 points only days after being held to 80 by the Celtics.
 Moussa Diabate has been a steady presence in the middle, leading the team with 9.1 rebounds per game, and he will be asked to hold the glass against a Phoenix front line that includes Bridges.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 6:00 PM ET 6 hours ago Suns last five: three wins and a scoring range from 96 to 133
 Phoenix has been home for its last five games, and the results show a team that can swing wildly from night to night.
 It lost 132-119 to Portland, beat Orlando 117-104, edged Houston 102-99, was blown out 122-96 by San Antonio and answered with a 133-110 win over the Clippers in its latest game. That is three wins in five, with the Suns scoring between 96 and 133 points. Their two defeats came by 13 and 26 points, which tells us this team has not been living in close games lately.
 The Clippers win is the freshest data point: a 23-point margin on the night after the 96-point game against San Antonio.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 6:00 PM ET 6 hours ago Devin Booker sets the tone at 25.1 points per game
 Everything in Phoenix starts with Devin Booker . He leads the Suns in both scoring (25.1 points per game) and assists (4.8), so he is the player who gets to the middle of the floor, collapses the defense and decides who gets the shot.
 Miles Bridges adds the toughness on the glass at 7.4 rebounds per game, and the pair gives Phoenix a clear balance between a primary creator and a physical forward who finishes in transition.
 Against a Charlotte rotation missing its two leading playmakers, the Suns have every reason to push the pace early and cash in Hornets turnovers for easy points in the open floor. Booker also owns the Suns' best assist number, so the first few possessions tell us whether Charlotte is sending a second defender at him.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 6:00 PM ET 6 hours ago Hornets walk in without three of their top guards and wings
 Charlotte's injury report is the loudest storyline before tip-off. Brandon Miller (groin), Kon Knueppel (hamstring) and Dennis Schroder (hamstring) are all listed as out.
 Miller leads the Hornets in scoring at 20.6 points per game, and Schroder leads them in assists at 4.9, so the two names who usually decide how Charlotte creates offense are both in street clothes. That puts extra usage on whoever starts in the backcourt and on a bench that has been asked to do a lot lately.
 Phoenix has one absence on its own list: center Mark Williams is out with a shoulder injury, which thins the Suns' frontcourt depth behind their starters.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 6:00 PM ET 6 hours ago Suns host Hornets in Phoenix, tip-off at 9:00 p.m. ET
 Welcome to VAVEL's live coverage of Charlotte Hornets at Phoenix Suns from the Mortgage Matchup Center. Tip-off is set for 9:00 p.m. ET (7:00 p.m. in Phoenix, where Arizona stays on Mountain Standard Time), which is 03:00 on Friday in Madrid.
 Two sub-.500 teams meet with plenty to prove. The Phoenix Suns are 4-6 on the season and 4-3 at home, while the Charlotte Hornets arrive at 4-7 with a 1-3 mark on the road. Oddsmakers have Phoenix as 6.5-point favorites with the total at 214.5.
 We will track every basket, run and rotation change as the game unfolds.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
